d.why: Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Fiddler on the Loose', where he is the target the episode is about: the Fiddler attacks his band to extort a ransom from him, and he unmasks the beaten Fiddler as Otto.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Spiderman Vs. Desparado', where he is the villain of the week, robbing banks with hypnotic guns from a flying robot horse.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Cloud City of Gold', where he is the episode's villain, the conquistador who captures the crash survivors and fires on Spider-Man.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Cold Storage', where he is the villain of the week, a diamond smuggler who locks Spider-Man in a freezer.
On screen in two Spider-Man (1967) episodes: 'Sub-Zero for Spidey' (S1 1B, with the Plutonians) and 'The Terrible Triumph of Dr. Octopus' (S1 17A), where Doctor Octopus steals his Nullifier.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'The Vanishing Doctor Vespasian', where he is the title villain who turns invisible to rob a bank and destroy Spider-Man.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Spider-Man Meets Skyboy', where he is the kidnap victim the episode is about, and he is the father of Skyboy (Jan), who has a file and drives that episode.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Phantom from the Depths of Time', where he is the villain of the week, enslaving people at his island castle with robot bugs.
On screen in two Spider-Man (1967) episodes: 'Never Step on a Scorpion' (S1 5A), where he creates the Scorpion, and 'Sting of the Scorpion' (S1 20A), where the Scorpion trashes his lab.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Spider-Man Meets Skyboy', where he is the episode's villain who kidnaps Dr. Caldwell.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'The Night of the Villains', where it is one of Parafino's three wax dummies, sent after Spider-Man in one short scene; Parafino is the episode's villain.
On screen in two Spider-Man (1967) episodes: 'The One-Eyed Idol' (S1 9A), robbing Jameson, and 'Fountain of Terror' (S1 18A), holding Dr. Connors in Florida.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Vine', where she is Peter's friend who is with him when the seed is released; the episode turns on the plant and the professor, not on her.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'The Night of the Villains', where it is one of Parafino's three wax dummies, robbing a bank in one short scene; Parafino is the episode's villain.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Fifth Avenue Phantom', where she is one of the Phantom's robot henchwomen who helps set Spider-Man up; the Phantom is the episode's villain.
On screen in two Spider-Man (1967) episodes as the fake Molemen leader: 'Menace from the Bottom of the World' (S2 5) and 'Spider-Man Battles the Molemen' (S2 7).
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Blueprint for Crime', where he and Cowboy are the thieves the episode is about, stealing the blueprints for the Plotter until Spider-Man lures and catches the gang.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Pardo Presents', where he is the title villain who hypnotizes an audience and becomes a giant energy cat.

Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Neptune's Nose Cone' (the later 'Down to Earth' reuses the footage with a different character), where she is the captive the natives mean to sacrifice and Spider-Man's rescue of her is the climax.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'The Peril of Parafino', where he is the escaped con Parafino uses as wax bait; Parafino is the villain and Melvin only revives at the end to attack him.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'The Scourge of the Scarf', where he is the title villain robbing the rich with illusions and laughing gas.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Cloud City of Gold', where he is the professor among the crash survivors whom DeVargas captures and Spider-Man frees; he is a companion, not what the episode turns on.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Diamond Dust', where he is the villain of the week whose men in gorilla suits rob a college museum.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Knight Must Fall', where he is the villain of the week, a knight on a crime spree with an electrified lance.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Criminals in the Clouds', where he is the episode's villain who kidnaps Roy Robinson for an invisibility formula.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'Super Swami', where he is the title villain faking a vanishing bridge and a snowstorm.
Only in Spider-Man (1967) 'The Slippery Dr. Von Schlick', where he is the title villain stealing oil in his non-stick suit.
